hints: Compare the heard frequency of $20.0 \text{ Hz}$ with the source frequency of $30.0 \text{ Hz}$ to decide if the waves are stretched or compressed.
Recall that for a source moving directly away, the observed wavelength is longer than $v/f_s$ because the source follows each wave, so $f_o = f_s v/(v+v_s)$ with $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Substitute $20.0 = 30.0 \times 330/(330+v_s)$ and solve for $v_s$ to check whether $110 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ or $165 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ fits.
walkthrough: Note the key data: source frequency $f_s = 30.0 \text{ Hz}$, observed frequency $f_o = 20.0 \text{ Hz}$, and wave speed $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Since $f_o < f_s$, the observed wavelength $\lambda_o = v/f_o$ is larger than the emitted wavelength, so the aircraft must be moving away from the stationary observer.
For a receding source, each successive wave is emitted further back, giving $\lambda_o = (v+v_s)/f_s$ and hence $f_o = v/\lambda_o = f_s v/(v+v_s)$.
Therefore $v_s = 495 - 330 = 165 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ away from the observer. This is option C.

options.A: Direction away is consistent with a lower observed frequency, but $110 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is too small and does not satisfy $f_o = f_s v/(v+v_s)$.
options.B: Moving towards the observer would compress the waves and raise the observed frequency above $30.0 \text{ Hz}$, not lower it to $20.0 \text{ Hz}$.
options.C: A receding source stretches the observed wavelength so $20.0 \text{ Hz} < 30.0 \text{ Hz}$, and $v_s = 165 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ satisfies the Doppler equation.
options.D: $165 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is the correct speed magnitude, but motion towards the observer would give an observed frequency greater than $30.0 \text{ Hz}$.
